newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian parliament to begin budget processing.
newsitem.headline: Australian parliament to begin budget processing.

text.p: The Australian government's budget bills will begin appearing in parliament over the next two weeks with debate expected in the spring session, which begins in late August.
Implementation of several budget measures not requiring legislation has started already.

These measures include plans to increase effficiency in the health sector, the continuation of funding for the Australian Film Finance Corp, and the outsourcing of the government's computer requirements.
(A near-comprehensive review of major budget measures and where they stand appears in an accompanying report.)

Priority will go to the budget measures that take effect from January 1998. Government officials expect some of those measures to be introduced into parliament in the next two weeks, which is the last fortnight of sittings before parliament breaks for winter.
But debate on these bills is not expected until parliament resumes for the spring session, when several budget measures due to take effect in July 1998 are also likely to be introduced.
With the introduction of so many measures still months away, most budget bills have not even been drafted yet.

"Effectively, there may not be any advice on the administration and what form they are going to take until November because they're not time sensitive as such," a spokesman for Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp told Reuters.

Included in the measures not due to take effect until July 1, 1998, and therefore expected in parliament later rather than sooner, was the cornerstone of the budget -- the 15 percent tax rebate on earnings from savings.

This particular measure is also likely to face the toughest battle through the non-government dominated upper house of parliament, the Senate, as the opposition and minor parties have all earmarked it for closer scrutiny.
